conversations.title: Summer Trip to Kyoto
conversations.scene: Two friends discuss a family trip planned for summer vacation.
conversations.sampleContext: Hana asks Kenta about his summer vacation plans, and he describes a bus trip to Kyoto.

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: けんたさん、今年の夏休みは何をしますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 家族と京都へ行きますよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 京都ですか。いいですね。初めてですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいえ、去年も行きました。でも、弟は初めてです。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: バスで行きますか。一日かかりますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: はい、バスです。でも、一日じゃありません。八時間かかります。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 八時間ですか。時間がかかりますね。何日から何日までですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 八月の三日から七日までです。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: いいですね。私も京都へ行きたいです。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: じゃあ、さ来年、私の家族と行きましょう。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Kenta, what will you do this summer vacation?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: I'm going to Kyoto with my family.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Kyoto? How nice. Is it your first time?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: No, I went last year too. But it's my little brother's first time.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Are you going by bus? Does it take a whole day?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Yes, by bus. But not a whole day — it takes eight hours.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Eight hours! That takes a long time. From what day to what day?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: From August third to the seventh.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: That's great. I want to go to Kyoto too.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Then the year after next, let's go with my family.

listeningQuestions: Where is Kenta going for summer vacation, and with whom?
Is this Kenta's first trip there?
For whom is it the first time?
How are they traveling, and how long does the trip take?
What are the dates of the trip?
What does Kenta suggest for the year after next?
answerKey: He is going to Kyoto with his family.
No, he also went last year.
It is the first time for his younger brother.
By bus; it takes eight hours.
From August third to August seventh.
That Hana come along with his family to Kyoto the year after next.

conversations.title: Bath Time for Taro
conversations.scene: A mother tells her son it is time for his bath and bed.
conversations.sampleContext: It is nine at night, and Yuki reminds her son Taro about the family's evening routine.

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 太郎、時計を見てください。もう九時ですよ。お風呂の時間です。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ええ…まだ遊びたいです。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: いいえ。毎晩、九時はお風呂の時間ですよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: はい、はい。じゃあ、お風呂へ行きます。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 服とその靴下は、この箱に入れてくださいね。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: はい。お母さん、今晩は何時に寝ますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 十時ですよ。毎晩、十時にベッドへ行きます。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: じゃあ、お風呂、そして十時にベッドですね。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: そうです。あ、お風呂の戸も閉めてくださいね。そして、毎朝六時に起きますよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ええ、六時ですか…はい、お母さん。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Taro, look at the clock. It's already nine o'clock. It's bath time.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Awww... I still want to play.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: No. Nine o'clock is bath time every night.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Okay, okay. I'll go to the bath then.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Put your clothes and those socks in this box, please.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Okay. Mom, what time do I go to sleep tonight?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Ten o'clock. Every night you go to bed at ten.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: So, bath first, then bed at ten, right?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: That's right. Oh, and please close the bath door too. And you get up at six every morning.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Ehh, six o'clock...? Yes, Mom.

listeningQuestions: What time is it when the conversation starts, and how does the mother point it out?
What does Taro want to keep doing?
Where should Taro put his clothes and socks?
What time does Taro go to bed every night?
What does the mother ask Taro to close?
What time must Taro get up every morning?
answerKey: It is nine o'clock; she tells him to look at the clock.
In the box (that she points to).

conversations.title: The New Apartment
conversations.scene: A man shows a friend around his new apartment.
conversations.sampleContext: Nao visits Naoki's new apartment for the first time and asks about the rooms and neighbors.

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: なおさん、ここが私の新しいアパートです。どうぞ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 失礼します。いいアパートですね。先月からですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: はい、先月の十日からここにいます。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: そうですか。もう一月ですね。部屋は大きいですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 部屋は小さいです。でも、窓が大きいですから、いいですよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: そうですね。トイレとお風呂はどこですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: あちらです。玄関の隣です。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 隣の部屋には、どなたがいますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 学生がいますよ。いい人です。時々、話します。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: いいですね。私もこのアパートが好きです。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Nao, this is my new apartment. Come in.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Excuse me. It's a nice apartment. Have you been here since last month?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Yes, I've been here since the tenth of last month.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: I see. So it's been a month already. Is the room big?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: The room is small. But the window is big, so it's nice.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: True. Where are the toilet and the bath?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Over there. Next to the entrance.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Who lives in the room next door?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: A student. A nice person. We talk sometimes.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: That's great. I like this apartment too.

listeningQuestions: Since when has Naoki lived in this apartment?
About how long has he lived there so far?
Is the room big or small, and why does Naoki still like it?
Where are the toilet and bath located?
Who lives in the room next door?
How often does Naoki talk with the neighbor?
answerKey: Since the tenth of last month.
The room is small, but the window is big, so it's nice.
Over there, next to the entrance.
A student, who is a nice person.

conversations.title: New Skirt, Old Shirt
conversations.scene: Two friends chat about their clothes and favorite colors.
conversations.sampleContext: Sho notices Ai's new skirt, and they compare their clothes and colors.

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: あいさん、こんにちは。あ、そのスカートは新しいですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: はい、新しいです。姉からです。先週、私の誕生日でしたから。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいですね。赤いスカートですね。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: はい、私は赤が好きです。翔さんのシャツは青いですね。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ええ。でも、このシャツは古いですよ。おととしから着ています。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: そうですか。でも、いい青ですよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ありがとうございます。私は青が好きです。冬のコートも青いですよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: そうですか。靴も青いですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいえ、靴は赤いです。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: ええ、赤い靴ですか。見たいです。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Hello, Ai. Oh, is that skirt new?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Yes, it's new. It's from my older sister. Because last week was my birthday.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Nice! A red skirt, huh.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Yes, I like red. Your shirt is blue, isn't it, Sho?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Yeah. But this shirt is old. I've been wearing it since the year before last.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Really? But it's a nice blue.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Thanks. I like blue. My winter coat is blue too.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Is that so? Are your shoes blue too?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: No, my shoes are red.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: What, red shoes? I want to see them!

listeningQuestions: Who gave Ai the new skirt, and why?
What color is Ai's new skirt?
How long has Sho been wearing his shirt?
What color does Sho like, and what other clothing item of his is that color?
What color are Sho's shoes?
What does Ai say she wants to do at the end?
answerKey: Her older sister gave it to her, because it was Ai's birthday last week.
He likes blue, and his winter coat is also blue.
She wants to see his red shoes.
vocabularyUsed: ありがとうございます

conversations.title: Free on Saturday?
conversations.scene: Two friends make plans to hang out on the weekend.
conversations.sampleContext: Sakura invites Ken to her house on Saturday afternoon, and they confirm the details.

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: けんさん、今週の土曜日は暇ですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 月曜日から金曜日までは時間がありません。でも、土曜日の午後は暇ですよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: じゃあ、午後、うちに来ませんか。友達と遊びますよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいですね。何時からですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 二時からです。晩御飯もうちで食べましょう。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ありがとうございます。さくらさんは、日曜日は何をしますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: 日曜日は毎週、家族と晩御飯を食べます。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいですね。じゃあ、土曜日の二時に行きます。バスで行きますね。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: はい。じゃあ、土曜日に。さようなら。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: さようなら。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Ken, are you free this Saturday?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: From Monday to Friday I have no time. But Saturday afternoon I'm free.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Then, won't you come to my house in the afternoon? We'll hang out with friends.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Sounds good. From what time?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: From two o'clock. Let's have dinner at my place too.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Thank you. Sakura, what do you do on Sundays?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: On Sundays, every week, I eat dinner with my family.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: That's nice. Then I'll come at two on Saturday. I'll go by bus.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Okay. See you Saturday. Goodbye.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Goodbye.

listeningQuestions: When during the week does Ken have no free time?
When exactly is Ken free this week?
What is the plan for Saturday afternoon?
What time does it start, and what meal is included?
What does Sakura do every Sunday?
How will Ken travel to Sakura's house?
answerKey: To come to Sakura's house and hang out with friends.
It starts at two o'clock, and they will also eat dinner at her house.
She eats dinner with her family every week.
vocabularyUsed: ありがとうございます

conversations.title: The Lost Bag
conversations.scene: A woman who lost her bag asks a passerby where the police box is.
conversations.sampleContext: Miki realizes her bag is missing and stops a man on the street for help.

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: すみません。あの、交番はどこにありますか。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 交番ですか。あの角にありますよ。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: ありがとうございます。あの、私のかばんがありません。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: ええ、かばんですか。大きいかばんですか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: いいえ、小さい青いかばんです。鍵と万年筆を入れました。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: 鍵もですか。それはよくないですね。バスで来ましたか。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: はい、今朝、バスで来ました。…ああ、バスですね。バスにありますね。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: そうですね。じゃあ、あの交番の人と話してください。

text.speaker: Speaker 1
text.japanese: はい、そうします。どうもありがとうございます。

text.speaker: Speaker 2
text.japanese: いいえ。あの角の交番ですよ。じゃあ、失礼します。

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Excuse me. Um, where is the police box?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: The police box? It's at that corner over there.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Thank you. Um, my bag is missing.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Oh no, your bag? Is it a big bag?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: No, it's a small blue bag. I put my key and a fountain pen in it.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Your key too? That's not good. Did you come by bus?

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Yes, I came by bus this morning. ...Ah, the bus! It must be on the bus.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Right. Then please talk to the person at that police box.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 1
englishTranslation.english: Yes, I'll do that. Thank you very much.

englishTranslation.speaker: Speaker 2
englishTranslation.english: Not at all. It's the police box on that corner. Well, excuse me.

listeningQuestions: What two things is the woman looking for in this conversation?
Where is the police box?
How does she describe her bag?
What did she put inside the bag?
How did she travel this morning, and why does that matter?
What does the man advise her to do?
answerKey: The police box and her missing bag.
It is a small, blue bag.
A key and a fountain pen.
She came by bus this morning, so the bag is probably still on the bus.
To go talk to the person at the police box on the corner.
vocabularyUsed: ありがとうございます
